messages:
maria: Heads-up — canary for token-budget governor v2 on route:search-prod. After the kernel switchover to opt-quant-fp8 the p95 jumped ~30ms across the canary hosts :thinking: saw the first spike ~1700UTC. putting quick profile + logs inline.

maria: ```profiling summary
kernel: opt-quant-fp8
sample: seq=32, tokens=48
avg kernel launch overhead: 1.8ms (prev opt-fp16 0.9ms)
kernel exec: 12.0ms (prev 10.5ms)
avg microbatch tokens: 34 (prev 48)
kv cache hitrate: 86% (prev 92%)
p95 overall: 240ms (prev 210ms)
```

kevin: Can you paste the batcher metrics & token-budget targets? Sounds like smaller microbatches + higher kernel launch cost -> p95. Also did queue policy flip recently?

maria: Quick config snapshot from the canary hosts:

maria: ```queue_policy:
  mode: fair_share
  fairness_window_ms: 10
  route_weights:
    search-prod: 1
    chat-prod: 2
token_budget_targets:
  gold: 100
  silver: 60
  bronze: 30
```

sasha: My hunch: opt-quant-fp8 reduces per-token throughput at short seq lengths because kernel-launch overhead dominates. If the batcher is forming smaller microbatches (avg tokens down) that amplifies the extra launch cost. Also KV hitrate drop suggests prefix caching missed more often — could be due to more route splitting or different routing keys.

ivor: We did flip fair_share from latency_guard -> fair_share last night to improve fairness across tiers. That lowers per-route token-budget headroom; search-prod now hits its cap earlier and backs off, which explains smaller batches. I flagged it in the change-log.

danielle: Short-term mitigation: bump token_budget_targets for gold on search-prod and increase batching window to let more requests coalesce. Proposed quick canary: gold=140, fairness_window_ms=15, canary=10%.

pranav: CLI to canary what danielle suggested: 

pranav: ```bash
rdwctl rollout batcher --route search-prod --set token_budget_gold=140 --set fairness_window_ms=15 --canary 10 --desc "temp mitigate p95 after opt-quant-fp8"
```

deploy-bot: Rollout queued: batcher-config update for route=search-prod -> token_budget_gold:140, fairness_window_ms:15. Canary 10% scheduled at 2700001200.

maria: Thanks — watching dashboards (+traces, kv-hit heatmaps). If p95 drops back near baseline I'll leave the canary to run 30m then we can iterate. :eyes:

kevin: If canary helps, we should either: 1) tune kernel selection to prefer fp16 for short seqs, or 2) make batcher aware of kernel launch cost when computing token_budget targets. The latter feels more robust.

sasha: Agreed. I can prototype a kernel-aware cost model that estimates launch overhead vs per-token cost and feeds a small multiplier into the token-budget governor. Will sketch a shim tomorrow.

ivor: FYI if kv-hitrate doesn't recover we may need to tweak routing keys so similar prefixes stay co-located (less cache churn).

maria: Will post canary metrics after 10min. If anyone wants the raw flame graphs I can paste them here.

pranav: Thx all — ping me if you want me to expand canary to 25% after initial check.

deploy-bot: Canary started at 2700001200 — 10% hosts. Monitoring: p95, kv_hit, microbatch_tokens. Will report auto-rollout decision after 30m.

maria: (10m update) Canary p95 back to ~216ms, avg microbatch tokens ~46, kv-hit 89% — improvement but not fully recovered. Leaving canary running.

kevin: Good signal. Keep tracking epoch by epoch and we can merge kernel-aware governor after prototype. :thumbsup:
